subject: Hitting the supercomputer wall limit before completion of minimization step

messages.author: Jatin Kashyap
messages.body:
Dear AMBER Community,
I am following the antechamber tutorial for my system (
https://ambermd.org/tutorials/basic/tutorial4b/index.html
).
During the minimization step, the wall clock limit was hit before completion of the minimization.
Shall it affect the structure of output files, and prevents me from going to next step i.e., equilibration.
Do I have to restart the minimization by decreasing the minimization steps so that it will be finished before hitting the wall limit OR I don’t have to worry about it, and I can continue with existing files, if yes then how?
Thank you.
——
Jatin Kashyap
Ph.D. Student
Dr. Dibakar Datta Group
Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering
New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT)
University Heights
Newark, NJ 07102-1982
Phone- (201)889-5783
Email- jk435.njit.edu

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
can you be more specific on which step you mean, and the length of the wall
clock limit?
If you mean the step "Minimize and Equilibrate the Sustiva-RT complex",
this should not take very long and you may want to check your output to see
if it is actually running. For debugging you might want to set ntpr=1 (but
do not do this for production runs).

messages.author: Jatin Kashyap
messages.body:
Yes, that is the step. But I am sorry for not bing clear at first, I am using my own system instead of Sustiva-RT complex. My HPC allows jobs to run for 24 hrs.
And I am performing minimization for 2000 steps but the last step I can see in output file is 1057 before it is terminated my HPC’s job scheduler.
Can I just go ahead and use the existing .ncrst file for MD run?
Thank you.
——

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
it's hard to say if the structure is ok or not. you might want to visually
inspect it based on your knowledge of the system, especially the ligand.
does it look ok?
are the energies ok in the minimization output? did it get stopped by the
wallclock, or had it gotten stuck before the 24 hours was reached?
